clue.text: Such language — whip the boy!

parts.note: the cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is an old naval whip
Alan is a stock boy's name

explanation.surface: An angry cry to punish a boy for using bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such language' points back to the whole clue: the cat whips the boy, and the result names a language of north-east Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalan is the tongue spoken in Catalonia, Barcelona's region of Spain.

clue.text: A novel to write, boy

parts.note: to pen a letter is to write it
Dennis is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a lad should write a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel is Thackeray's 1850 story of a young man's career.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's Victorian book about a young gentleman bears this title.

clue.text: Off-cuts the firm used for wall covering

indicators.note: off means bad or awry, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company recycles its leftover scraps as a coating for walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off-cuts' reads as scraps, but 'Off' is the anagram signal for CUTS, giving STUC; then CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster rendered onto walls and ceilings.

clue.text: He has an idea but combines it with others

indicators.note: combines means the letters of the two words are mixed together into one new arrangement

explanation.surface: A thinker shares his notion with colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combines' mixes IT and OTHERS together into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who forms hypotheses or speculative explanations is a man with ideas.

clue.text: In a volatile state, using painting medium, people correspond with one another

parts.note: tempera is paint bound with egg yolk
men are people
two accounts that tally agree with each other

explanation.surface: An artist working in a particular medium while people write letters back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspond' suggests letter-writing, but it means agree, as figures do when they tally.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting from a moody, excitable disposition is behaving unpredictably, in a volatile way.

clue.text: Once a worker in 26 across, now conducting the trial

parts.note: ex means former, once
26 across is a coal mine, and a man working there digs coal

explanation.surface: A former pitman who now presides over a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now' contrasts with 'Once' in the surface and is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sets and invigilates a test or inspection runs that trial.

clue.text: Cross when I left in indebted condition

indicators.note: in places the first letter and the abbreviation inside the colour of debt

parts.note: an account in the red is in debt

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at being left owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in the red' means overdrawn, so RED stands for the indebted condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyed or angered is the adjectival sense of cross.

clue.text: Support us in a spot

indicators.note: in says one word goes inside the other here

parts.note: a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: A plea for help from people in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a spot' looks like trouble, but it is a mark, STAIN, with US put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear up or keep going is to uphold, a synonym of support.

clue.text: Hidden, as talent may be

indicators.note: may be suggests the word could be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Ability that lies undiscovered within someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also works as a plain statement: talent is often dormant until found.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent is present but not yet showing, so concealed.

clue.text: Set meals suitable for vegetarians

indicators.note: suitable here hints the letters are made to suit, rearranged into a fitting order

explanation.surface: A restaurant's fixed-price menus that cater for those who avoid flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set meals' reads as a fixed menu, but both words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes without flesh are what non-carnivores eat.

clue.text: Useful sort of headgear, they say, but may put you at a disadvantage

definitions.text: may put you at a disadvantage

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are spoken, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: a handy cap would be convenient hat-wear

explanation.surface: A practical hat might seem a good idea, yet it could hold you back.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'handy cap' and you hear the word for an impediment.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment or burden imposed in a race or golf hampers the person carrying it.

clue.text: A national, I get in and out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describing their own comings and goings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IN AND into NDIAN after the single I.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the subcontinent's largest country is one of its nationals.

clue.text: Boor ran off, coming to dead end inside, but finding this exit

indicators.note: inside means the letter goes within the jumbled letters
off means disordered, so the two words' letters are mixed up
end means the final letter of the word dead is taken

explanation.surface: A rude fellow flees down a blind alley and escapes through a farm building's opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' jumbles BOOR RAN; 'dead end' gives D, placed 'inside' that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A large door on a farm building lets animals and carts out, a way of leaving.

clue.text: One has to be right, with tirade that's rambling

parts.note: a means one
taken as the verb be
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: Insisting you are correct while delivering a long harangue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' is the definition in its sense of straying from the expected course.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviating or wandering from the normal path is the core sense of the word.

clue.text: Sports training on Sunday, they may cause a traffic hold-up

definitions.text: they may cause a traffic hold-up

parts.note: roadwork is the running a boxer does to train

explanation.surface: Weekend athletes jogging on the road hold up the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: Roadwork is boxers' and athletes' training run along roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs to a highway close lanes and bring cars to a standstill.

clue.text: Green when you pull back over libel action

indicators.note: over places the first part above the second in a down entry
back means the word for pull is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to lug is to pull or drag

indicators.note: action stirs the letters into motion, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A naive person drops a libel lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LUG to GUL; 'action' rearranges LIBEL into LIBLE, and 'over' puts GUL above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced and easily fooled, naive.

clue.text: Dampening needed with more crumpled suit inside

indicators.note: inside means the jumbled letters go within the other word
crumpled means creased out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrinkled suit needs to be sprayed with water before ironing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' jumbles SUIT into ISTU, which goes 'inside' MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wetness or damp is what a dampening imparts.

clue.text: Seasoning duck with orange purée

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, O

indicators.note: a purée is mashed up, so the letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Duck à l'orange flavoured with a fruit sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is cricket's nought, O; 'purée' mashes ORANGE into REGANO.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram's Mediterranean cousin is a herb used to flavour food.

clue.text: Nice day, perhaps, for a murder

definitions.note: a phrase describing a poison as something used for a killing

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A pleasant day chosen as the perfect occasion for a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges NICE DAY; the definition is loose, a poison used for a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: This fast-acting poison is a classic means of killing in detective fiction.

clue.text: Wonderful period of time — all too short

definitions.text: Wonderful period of time — all too short

parts.words: Wonderful period of time — all too short
parts.note: alludes to the saying about a sensation that is soon forgotten, a wonder lasting only just over a week

explanation.surface: A lament that a marvellous time passed too quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'nine days' wonder' is something that causes a stir and is quickly forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the brief span of a short-lived sensation.

clue.text: Two lads get together, as usual

parts.note: Norm and Al are both short boys' names, one lad each
Norm and Al are both short boys' names, one lad each

explanation.surface: Two boys meeting up as they always do.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid as printed reads NORMAN, but the clue plainly builds NORM + AL, a word for usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard or customary, the way things ordinarily are, is the sense here.

clue.text: About to queue for sale

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a tail is a line of waiting people, a queue

explanation.surface: Shoppers about to line up for the bargains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queue' here is the noun tail, the line behind a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling goods to the public in small quantities is the trade sense of the word.

clue.text: Record a girl's name — a student

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
L is the learner plate, a student driver

explanation.surface: Writing down a girl's name, along with a pupil's.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A single year's entry in a chronicle is a written account.

clue.text: Cast iron bar first engineer sent flying

indicators.note: cast means thrown or moulded anew, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for engineer

explanation.surface: A metal rod was the first thing an engineer threw through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast iron' looks like the metal, but 'Cast' rearranges IRON BAR; 'first' puts that before E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in flight, carried through the air, has been sent flying.

clue.text: Manful character?

parts.note: read manful as full of man, someone whose stomach is full of people he has eaten

explanation.surface: A question about someone brave and manly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manful' usually means courageous; here it means having eaten humans.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who eats human flesh would be full of man.

clue.text: For self-defence, form a circle, putting one youngster inside

indicators.note: inside means the two pieces go within the outer pair of letters

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle
I is the Roman numeral one
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: Instructions for a class of children practising martial arts in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Form A and O, then put I KID 'inside' them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese martial art using an attacker's own force is a system of self-protection.

clue.text: Line on dog that's mine

indicators.note: on means the line piece is placed after the dog in an across entry

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Someone claiming the dog on the leash belongs to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive but is a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal pit and its workings are a type of mine.
